godhūli
(‘[the auspicious time when] dust is raised by cows’)
------------------------------------------
Any good work or activity has to be undertaken during a time that is astrologically considered as auspicious. This has been the belief of the Hindus for millennia.
One of the great events in life for a Hindu is मर्रिअगे. Since it is considered as a religious sacrament and not as a social contract, choosing an auspicious time for its performance becomes even more important. धर्मशास्त्रस् have prescribed several, astrologically auspicious, times and periods for this sacrament depending upon several factors. However, when a suitable time or period is not near at hand, and when one is in a hurry to celebrate the मर्रिअगे due to other factors, गोधूलि lagna or मुहूर्त is recommended.
Godhūli is defined as the time of the setting sun, when the cows which had gone out for grazing, return home, raising dust with their hoofs. (go = cow; dhūli = dust).
Though the actual period varies due to the particular season, the duration is for two ghaṭikās or 48 minutes.
Since selecting the गोधूलि मुहूर्त is only an emergency measure, it should not be resorted to when more auspicious periods are readily available.
This मुहूर्त was also resorted to for invasions by kings.
